To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the membrane electrical properties of oocyte plasma membrane are affected by the maturation stage, and not by the age of the animal.

the acquisition of meiosis and developmental competence of oocytes from juvenile or adult individuals was not related to differences in membrane electrical properties, cytoplasmic calcium stores or IP3 sensitivity.
the oocyte quality, as assessed in relation to membrane and calcium store parameters and to incidence of cell apoptosis in the cumulus, was not affected by age of the donor but by maturational stage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of oocyte maturation in relation to oocyte age, that is, juvenile vs. adult oocytes and the evaluation of differences between species.
the evaluation of differences in the plasma membrane and cytosolic properties of oocytes from juvenile and adult individuals.
the study of the acquisition of oocyte meiotic and developmental potential in relation to oocyte age and maturational stages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

all the examined parameters are greatly affected by the oocyte maturational stage and minor differences are due to age‐dependent oocyte quality, at plasma membrane level, to conductance, peak of activation current and L‐type Ca currents, at cytoplasmic level, to calcium stores and sensitivity to IP3, and to the occurrence of apoptosis in cumuli cells.

the oocyte quality, in terms of membrane electrical properties and calcium stores and IP 3 sensitivity, was greater in adult oocytes than in juvenile oocytes, but that the incidence of apoptosis of cumulus cells was greater in adult cumulus cells.

all the examined parameters, both membrane and intracellular ones, were greatly affected by oocyte maturation, whereas minor differences, if any, were due to the age of donor, which is a parameter that may be used to evaluate the oocyte quality in relation to species and individuals, and may also be considered a useful indicator of the oocyte quality.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the oocyte quality is mainly affected by maturational stage and not by donor age.

oocyte quality, at plasma membrane and cytosol levels, is affected more by the maturative stage than by the donor’s age, but that cumulus cells are more prone to apoptosis in adult oocytes than in juvenile oocytes.
oocytes are very sensitive to maturational stage and that the differences between juvenile and adults are not as important as previously thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the acquisition of meiocyte competence is a complex process that requires time to occur.
all the examined parameters are strongly affected by the matriation stage and minor differences are due to age‐ related oocyte quality.
all the examined parameters, except for the resting potential, were greatly affected by maturational stage rather than by age‐related oocytes quality.
